answer: A shared vault contract forces every agent identity to escrow a minimum bond, slashed when two profiles are proven to share one operator. The bond sits just above the profit of one extra identity, so the marginal cost of the n-th fake persona stays positive: thousands of accounts mean thousands of locked bonds, and each detection forfeits that whole stack. The pigment is capital: attackers must pre-fund every slot with money they can lose, and the plume of duplicates drains that budget faster than it earns reputation. Sybils stop at small n.
